name: Geography trivia (easy)
description: 50 easy questions about countries, capitals, rivers, mountains, landmarks, maps. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which river flows north through Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean Sea?
items.explain: The Nile flows north through Uganda, South Sudan, Sudan and Egypt, then drains into the Mediterranean near Cairo. It is generally regarded as the world's longest river.

items.question: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?
items.explain: The Colorado River began cutting through the rock layers of the Colorado Plateau about six million years ago and carved the canyon.

source.title: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?

items.question: On which continent does the Amazon River flow?
items.explain: The Amazon is the greatest river of South America. It drains roughly two-fifths of the continent.

items.question: Which river carries more water than any other river in the world?
items.explain: The Amazon is the largest drainage system in the world by volume of flow and basin area. Its discharge exceeds that of the next nine largest rivers.

items.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
items.explain: The Pacific covers about one-third of the globe. It has twice the area of the Atlantic, the next largest ocean.

items.question: Which trench in the Pacific Ocean holds the deepest known point on Earth?
items.explain: The Mariana Trench, near the Mariana Islands, reaches about 36,201 feet (11,034 m). That is deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

items.question: Which of Earth's oceans is the smallest by surface area?
items.explain: Britannica ranks the Pacific as largest, then the Atlantic, with the Arctic the smallest.

items.question: The explorer Ferdinand Magellan gave the Pacific Ocean a name that means what?
items.explain: Magellan called the ocean El Mar Pacifico, which means "the peaceful sea."

items.question: About what fraction of Earth's surface is covered by ocean?
items.explain: Oceans cover almost three-fourths of Earth. Their area is more than double that of all the continents combined.

items.question: What is the highest mountain in the world above sea level?
items.explain: Mount Everest reaches about 29,032 feet (8,849 m), making it the highest mountain in the world.

items.question: Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and which other country?
items.explain: Everest sits on the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.

items.question: Mount Everest is part of which mountain range?
items.explain: Everest stands on the crest of the Great Himalayas of southern Asia.

items.question: Who made the first recorded climb to the summit of Mount Everest, in 1953?
items.explain: New Zealander Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay were the first to summit Everest, in 1953.

items.question: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest peak in Africa?
items.explain: Kilimanjaro, at 5,895 m, is Africa's highest peak and stands in Tanzania.

items.question: Denali, the highest peak in North America, is located in which U.S. state?
items.explain: Denali, also known as Mount McKinley, is the highest peak in North America and lies in Alaska.

source.title: The Seven Summits - Highest Mountain on Each Continent

items.question: Which desert is the largest hot desert in the world?
items.explain: The Sahara, across northern Africa, is the world's largest hot desert.

items.question: Which of these countries contains part of the Sahara?
items.explain: The Sahara covers parts of Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Egypt, Mauritania, Mali, Niger, Chad and Sudan.

items.question: If cold deserts are counted as well as hot ones, which is the largest desert on Earth?
items.explain: A desert is defined by low rainfall, not heat. Antarctica covers about 14.2 million km², far more than the Sahara.

source.title: Top 10 Largest Deserts in the World (Ranked by Area)

items.question: The name "Sahara" comes from an Arabic word meaning what?
items.explain: Sahara comes from the Arabic word ṣaḥrāʾ, which means "desert."

items.question: Which country is the largest in the world by area?
items.explain: Russia covers about 17 million square kilometres, by far the largest of any country.

items.question: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
items.explain: Vatican City covers just 0.17 square mile (0.44 sq km). Monaco is the next smallest.

source.title: List of the smallest countries by area

items.question: Vatican City is an enclave entirely surrounded by which city?
items.explain: Vatican City is an independent enclave within the city of Rome, Italy.

items.question: Which country is the largest in South America?
items.explain: Brazil is the largest country in South America. It occupies nearly half of the continent's land area.

items.question: Russia stretches across eastern Europe and the northern part of which other continent?
items.explain: Russia covers much of eastern Europe and all of northern Asia.

items.question: How many continents does Earth have, by the most common count?
items.explain: The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

items.question: Which is the largest continent on Earth by size?
items.explain: Asia is the largest continent, at about 44.6 million square kilometres.

items.question: Which is the smallest of Earth's seven continents?
items.explain: Ranked from largest to smallest, the continents end with Europe and then Australia, the smallest.

items.question: Which continent is the second largest, after Asia?
items.explain: Africa is the second-largest continent, covering more than three times the area of the United States.

items.question: What is the world's largest island?
items.explain: Britannica calls Greenland the world's largest island. Australia is about four times larger, but it counts as a continent.

items.question: In 1912 Alfred Wegener proposed that the continents were once joined in one huge landmass. What did he call it?
items.explain: Wegener named the single large landmass Pangaea. He suggested it split apart more than 200 million years ago.

items.question: What is the capital of Australia?
items.explain: Canberra, in the southeast, lies between the larger cities of Sydney and Melbourne.

source.title: What is the capital of Australia?

items.question: What is the capital of Canada?
items.explain: Ottawa is the capital of Canada.

items.question: What is the capital of Japan?
items.explain: Tokyo is the capital of Japan.

items.question: What is the capital of Greece?
items.explain: Athens is the capital of Greece.

items.question: What is the capital of Norway?
items.explain: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

items.question: What is the capital of Russia?
items.explain: Moscow is the capital of Russia.

items.question: What is the capital of China?
items.explain: Beijing is the capital of China.

source.title: world capitals at a glance - Students

items.question: What is the capital of India?
items.explain: New Delhi is the capital of India.

source.title: world capitals at a glance - Students

items.question: What is the capital of Egypt?
items.explain: Cairo is the capital of Egypt.

source.title: List of world capitals by countries

items.question: What is the capital of Argentina?
items.explain: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina.

source.title: World Capitals FULL LIST + Photos of all the Capital Cities in the World!

items.question: In which city is the Eiffel Tower?
items.explain: The Eiffel Tower is in Paris, the capital of France. It is among the most famous landmarks in the world.

items.question: Which French engineer designed the iron framework of the Statue of Liberty and a famous Paris tower?
items.explain: Gustave Eiffel built the Eiffel Tower in Paris between 1887 and 1889. His other major structures include the Statue of Liberty.

items.question: In which country is the Taj Mahal located?
items.explain: The Taj Mahal is in Agra, India. It is a white-marble mausoleum.

items.question: In which country is the Inca citadel of Machu Picchu?
items.explain: Machu Picchu is in the Cusco Region of Peru.

items.question: In which country is the ancient rock-carved city of Petra?
items.explain: Petra is an ancient city in Ma'an, Jordan, with buildings carved into sandstone cliffs.

items.question: In which country is the statue of Christ the Redeemer?
items.explain: Brazil's Statue of Christ the Redeemer was named one of the new seven wonders of the world in 2007.

source.title: New Seven Wonders of the World chosen

items.question: In which country are the Maya ruins of Chichén Itzá?
items.explain: Chichén Itzá is in the Yucatán region of Mexico.

items.question: Historically, the Great Wall of China was built to fortify which border of China?
items.explain: The wall was built to defend China's northern frontier against raiders and invaders.

source.title: Why was the Great Wall of China built?

items.question: In which U.S. state is the Grand Canyon?
items.explain: The Grand Canyon lies in the high plateau region of northwestern Arizona.

items.question: Which of the original Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is the only one still standing?
items.explain: The pyramids at Giza in Egypt are the only surviving structures from the original ancient wonders.

source.title: New Seven Wonders of the World chosen
